entry_conditions: Use two available causal 20 Hz observations in the world frame, preserving qpos[0:9] in radians/metres, qvel[9:18], TCP pose[18:25], red pose[25:32], blue pose[32:39] and goal xyz[41:47]; pose quaternions are wxyz. At original start fingers can be open at 0.040 m each and red stacked at z=0.060 m on blue at 0.020 m. At blue invocation, permit red still held over its negative-y pad with fingers around 0.0183 m and downward TCP/object motion. Inspected second-slice starts include red at z=0.209 m in demo10200 235 and 0.277 m in demo10204 230. There is no external role-tag input; the learned object-indexed belief uses physical state and its causal change and must not be artificially reset to empty/approaching blue. Prefer a warm observation pair; repeated initial-state padding provides no motion evidence.
exit_conditions: Transfer to carry/place when the selected object's elevation and motion with the TCP, approximately persistent TCP-object relative pose, and measured finger closure jointly support attached/lifting or initial carry. The recorded exit band is selected z about 0.28-0.32 m and total finger width about 0.03651-0.03652 m, with lateral motion sometimes continuing. For example demo10200 150 has red z=0.3082 m versus TCP 0.3096 m; demo10204 531 has blue z=0.2807 m versus TCP 0.2810 m. These are support references, not hard eligibility or learned-belief thresholds. A -1 command alone, one high TCP pose, or red reaching its pad is not sufficient evidence that selected-object acquisition is ready for carry handoff. No calibrated stopping head or externally returned belief is implemented.
overlap_role: Train and execute the full expanded transition, not merely a narrowly cut grasp. Acquisition/carry overlaps include open approach, finger closure, coupled lift and initial lateral carrying for both objects. The long red-placement/blue-acquisition overlap includes red held while descending, opening near the pad, empty vertical retreat and translation toward blue, then next approach. Inspected demo10200 overlap ranges are [80,180), [235,430), [440,540); demo10204 has [77,174), [230,418), [434,532). At demo10204 100 the fingers are still at 0.0204 m and closing, while demo10200 100 is already pinched but red remains supported. At demo10204 270 red is still pinched near the pad, 280 is opening, 290 is almost fully open and 310 retreats without red following. The policy learns all these action phases through diffusion and causal outcome supervision, with no instantaneous scripted contact reset.
successor_readiness: Supply the latest two ordered raw physical observations, including both objects and goals, to let the successor infer pinch, coupling and motion direction in the same world frame and common normalization. The inference agent should retain which object is selected and which is previous as invocation context, but this low-level forward has no role-tag channel and exports no recurrent latent state. Its six object-indexed modes replace the unavailable role-tag interface. Never pass future-derived phase labels as observations or contact truth. If the successor needs longer history, retain real past observations outside this policy rather than manufacture future evidence. Finger closure plus object following, not geometric height alone, is the useful carry-ready information.
failure_signatures: Potential warning signs are TCP rising without comparable selected-object rise, an abrupt change of TCP-object relative translation or orientation, fingers remaining open after a close command, an empty retreat that drags red, or alternating apparent association between red and blue. Check current finger positions as well as commands; the latter are not model deployment inputs. Successful held states can still have finger qvel near -0.020 and +0.026 m/s, so strict zero-velocity contact tests are unsupported. These signs are interpretation guidance, not a trained failure classifier or validated recovery controller. Belief oscillation can be studied offline but is not exposed by the fixed action-only forward API.
continuation_guidance: Continue this acquisition policy through incomplete closure and coupled upward lift; for blue entered early, let it first finish red descent, open, clear and approach blue. In the training continuation, pinch command -1 is maintained through lift and initial carry, while red release and empty retreat use +1; these are learned action patterns, never post-hoc command overrides. After the fixed eight-action execution prefix, reobserve actual finger and object state before extending the invocation or transferring. Do not change policy solely because red already satisfies its pad geometry while the gripper remains around it. The two-block completion contract alone determines task success; release, clearance, slow motion and sustained hold are not added success predicates.
limitations: Observed demonstrations and boundary/overlap summaries establish only on-path support. Two observations span 0.05 s; the proposed longer contact history and full semi-Markov durations are not available. The learned belief has a soft one-step transition preference and future-supervised predictions, not measured contact, persistent cross-call memory or a task planner. Future labels are training-only and belief confidence is uncalibrated on failures. No force/tactile sensing, IK, hard attachment constraint, guaranteed no-support disturbance or slip recovery is implemented. Arbitrary unobserved hand-object states, reversed task order or unseen delayed contact are outside demonstrated support. Physical modes do not replace caller intent for selecting another skill.
